desc: Thailand's largest retail group, running Central department stores, Tops supermarkets, Robinson and Power Buy, with Vietnam and Italy businesses.
markets: Thailand, Vietnam and Italy (Rinascente, Illum); expanding formats in Vietnam and Southeast Asia.
rationale: Brand building with affluent Thai and tourist shoppers; hospitality for luxury and sportswear partners at the Thai and Singapore races.

desc: Makes starches, sweeteners and texturizers from corn and other crops for food, beverage and industrial manufacturers worldwide.
markets: Sells to food makers across North America, South America, EMEA and Asia-Pacific; steady specialty-ingredient expansion.
rationale: Largely B2B ingredient supplier; limited consumer brand, so F1 hospitality use for food-customer relationships is plausible but weak.

desc: Australian retailer of consumer electronics, appliances and entertainment through JB Hi-Fi and The Good Guys stores in Australasia.
markets: Australia and New Zealand; no verified expansion plans beyond those markets.
rationale: Home-market brand with tech-product customers; Melbourne Grand Prix hospitality and electronics promotions fit locally, little global reach.

desc: Saudi retailer of electronics, books and office supplies through Jarir Bookstore outlets in Saudi Arabia, the Gulf and Egypt.
markets: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Qatar, Kuwait, Bahrain, Oman and Egypt; ongoing store growth in the Gulf.
rationale: Saudi Grand Prix in Jeddah offers local brand visibility with young, tech-minded Gulf consumers and electronics tie-ins.

desc: Makes home products including Moen faucets, Therma-Tru doors, Master Lock padlocks and Fiberon decking, sold mainly in North America.
markets: Mostly United States and Canada, with some sales in Europe and Asia; no verified expansion plans.
rationale: Master Lock and Moen have consumer brand recognition for US race-weekend promotions, but the business is largely domestic building products.

desc: Runs a chain of extreme-value discount stores in the eastern and central US selling overstock and closeout goods.
markets: United States only; adding new stores each year across more states.
rationale: Discount shopper base and thin margins make F1 spend an unnatural fit despite US Grand Prix visibility.

desc: Sports and fashion retail group owning Sports Direct, Flannels, House of Fraser and Evans Cycles, with stakes in other retailers.
markets: United Kingdom, Ireland and continental Europe; acquiring and upscaling premium fashion and sports retail brands.
rationale: UK home Grand Prix and premium fashion Flannels customers suit hospitality; Sports Direct sells licensed sportswear that could link to team merchandise.

desc: Japanese food maker best known for Cup Noodles and Chicken Ramen instant noodles, sold in dozens of countries.
markets: Japan, the US, Brazil, India, China, Europe and Southeast Asia; expanding Cup Noodles production overseas.
rationale: Global instant-noodle brand with strong Japanese and US youth appeal; Japanese Grand Prix at Suzuka offers a natural activation.

desc: Makes Reynolds Wrap foil, Hefty trash and storage bags and Presto cookware products sold mainly through US retailers.
markets: United States and Canada; no verified expansion plans.
rationale: Household staples with US mass-market reach; an F1 fan-engagement tie-in could support Reynolds Wrap in the US but is not obvious.

desc: Latin American retail group operating Jumbo and Santa Isabel supermarkets, Paris department stores, Easy home improvement and shopping malls.
markets: Chile, Argentina, Brazil, Peru, Colombia and the United States; expanding digital retail and malls.
rationale: Brand visibility with Latin American shoppers could connect to Sao Paulo and Mexico City races, though F1 is rarely used by grocers.

desc: Largest Japanese bakery company, making bread, pastries and confectionery under Yamazaki and Daily Yamazaki convenience store brands.
markets: Mostly Japan, with small operations in the US, Asia and Europe; no verified expansion plans.
rationale: Domestic bread maker with little marketing link to motorsport; Suzuka hospitality for staff or partners is the only plausible angle.

desc: Operates membership warehouse clubs under the PriceSmart name across Central America, the Caribbean and Colombia.
markets: Central America, the Caribbean and Colombia; opening new warehouse clubs in existing countries.
rationale: Latin American membership brand could reach regional fans around Mexico City and Brazil races, though marketing spend is modest.

desc: Portuguese retail group running Continente supermarkets, Worten electronics and Sport Zone stores, with telecom and shopping centre investments.
markets: Portugal, Spain and select international retail ventures; investing in digital retail and renewable energy.
rationale: Portugal's Algarve and Portimao circuit visibility could support Continente and Worten brand work, though the company is a domestic conglomerate.

desc: Belgian supermarket chain operating Colruyt, Okay and Bio-Planet stores, plus wholesale and fuel stations in Belgium, France and Luxembourg.
markets: Belgium, France and Luxembourg; no verified expansion plans.
rationale: Low-price positioning and domestic focus make F1 sponsorship an awkward fit, though Spa-Francorchamps is local.

desc: Brazilian protein and food producer merged from Marfrig and BRF, selling beef, poultry and processed foods in over 100 countries.
markets: Exports to Middle East, Asia and Europe, with brands such as Sadia, Perdigao and Seara; expanding Halal-processed foods.
rationale: Sao Paulo Grand Prix visibility for Sadia and Perdigao brands among Brazilian consumers and trade buyers from key export markets.

desc: Operates large-format warehouse stores selling hard-surface flooring, tile, stone and decor to homeowners and professionals across the United States.
markets: United States only; opening new warehouse stores yearly.
rationale: US flooring retailer with limited global appeal, but US race weekends offer builder and contractor hospitality.

desc: Asian retail group operating grocery stores, convenience stores and health and beauty shops including Wellcome, Cold Storage and Giant.
markets: Hong Kong, Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia and Cambodia; focused on food and convenience formats.
rationale: Singapore Grand Prix visibility for Cold Storage and Giant; Asian shopper base, though Jardine group sponsorship is rare.

desc: Makes recreational boats, marine engines and parts under Mercury Marine, Sea Ray and Boston Whaler brands for leisure customers.
markets: Sells boats and engines in North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific; investing in electric and autonomous boating.
rationale: Mercury Marine's engine engineering and Miami and Monaco-style yachting audiences suit a technology and premium-leisure tie-in.

desc: Indian packaged food and edible oil company, formerly Ruchi Soya, making Patanjali edible oils, flour, biscuits and wellness foods.
markets: India, with exports to the Gulf, Nepal and other markets; expanding palm oil and food retail.
rationale: Strong Indian consumer brand, though no Indian Grand Prix and its Ayurvedic marketing is tied to domestic values.

desc: World's largest maker of corn flour and tortillas, selling Maseca flour and Mission tortillas across the Americas, Europe and Asia.
markets: Operations in Mexico, the US, Central America, Europe, Asia and Oceania; expanding plants in US and Asia.
rationale: Mexico City Grand Prix and US Hispanic audiences give Maseca and Mission high-visibility brand-building opportunities.

desc: Operates Sprouts Farmers Market grocery stores in the United States focusing on fresh, natural and organic foods.
markets: United States only; opening around 30 new stores yearly.
rationale: Health-focused US grocer with little F1 use, though Austin and Miami races could connect with affluent fans.

desc: Japanese department store operator running Daimaru and Matsuzakaya stores, plus Parco shopping centres, real estate and credit-card businesses.
markets: Japan, with some Asian partnership projects; no verified expansion plans beyond inbound-tourist focus.
rationale: Suzuka visitors and affluent shoppers could connect to luxury partners, though the group has little motorsport marketing history.

desc: Indian value retail chain selling apparel, general merchandise and everyday consumer goods in hundreds of stores in smaller cities.
markets: India only; continuing to open new stores.
rationale: Domestic value retailer serving price-sensitive shoppers; no Indian race and limited marketing reason for F1.

desc: Makes Titleist golf balls, clubs and gear plus FootJoy golf shoes and gloves, sold in over 50 countries.
markets: North America, Europe, Japan, Korea and other Asian markets; premium golf brands growing in Asia.
rationale: Premium sporting brands with affluent audience could use F1 paddock hospitality and global-fan exposure, though golf has its own sponsorship ecosystem.

desc: Value retailer of general merchandise operating B&M and Heron Foods stores in the United Kingdom, plus B&M France.
markets: United Kingdom and France; continuing to open stores, particularly in France.
rationale: UK home Grand Prix reach, but discount image and cost focus make F1 a poor fit.

desc: Thai wholesale and retail group operating Makro cash-and-carry and Lotus's supermarkets in Thailand, Cambodia and Myanmar.
markets: Thailand, Cambodia and Myanmar; expanding Lotus's stores and Makro in Southeast Asia.
rationale: Part of the CP Group, which supports Thai Grand Prix interest; mass-market brand building is limited.

desc: Produces specialty vegetable oils and fats for chocolate, bakery, dairy and food service customers from plants worldwide.
markets: Sells to food makers in Europe, North America, Latin America and Asia; adding specialty-fat capacity.
rationale: Ingredient supplier selling business to business; F1 hospitality could host food-industry clients but offers little brand effect.

desc: Distributes specialty foods and ingredients to chefs and restaurants, serving fine-dining and hospitality customers across the United States and Canada.
markets: United States, Canada and the Middle East; growing through acquisitions and new distribution centres.
rationale: Chef and restaurant customers overlap with F1 hospitality caterers, but the company is a low-profile distributor.

desc: Japanese flour miller producing Nisshin flour, pasta, frozen foods and premixes, with operations in North America, Asia and Europe.
markets: Japan, Thailand, Canada, the US, New Zealand and other markets; expanding processed food abroad.
rationale: Pasta and frozen-food brand could use Suzuka and Miami visibility, but marketing is domestic and B2B.

desc: Israeli food and beverage company producing dairy, snacks, coffee and Sabra hummus, with plants in Israel, Europe and North America.
markets: Israel, the United States, Brazil and Europe; Sabra hummus and coffee growth overseas.
rationale: Sabra hummus has US retail reach; Miami and Austin races could build awareness, though marketing is mainly domestic.

desc: Japanese department store operator with Takashimaya stores in Japan and overseas in Singapore, Shanghai, Ho Chi Minh City and Bangkok.
markets: Japan, Singapore, China, Vietnam, Thailand and Malaysia; opening new overseas stores, notably in Southeast Asia.
rationale: Premium department stores in Singapore and Suzuka-area tourism could host luxury partners and affluent customers at races.

desc: French poultry producer selling Loue and Le Gaulois chicken and prepared poultry products, mainly to supermarkets in France and Europe.
markets: France and export markets in Europe and Africa; no verified expansion plans.
rationale: Domestic food supplier with little consumer marketing; French Grand Prix is absent, making F1 weak.

desc: Greek retailer of toys, baby products, home goods and sporting goods, operating Jumbo stores in Greece, Cyprus, Bulgaria and Romania.
markets: Greece, Cyprus, Bulgaria, Romania and Serbia; opening stores in Southeast Europe.
rationale: Toy and family brand could use F1 for family fan engagement, but Southeast Europe has no race.

desc: Japanese discount supermarket operator running Gyomu Super stores, which sell low-priced frozen food and bulk ingredients to households and restaurants.
markets: Japan, with a small overseas presence; no verified expansion plans.
rationale: Value-focused domestic retailer with minimal global ambitions or marketing culture suited to F1.

desc: Mexican retailer and financial group selling furniture, electronics and credit through Elektra stores and Banco Azteca across Latin America.
markets: Mexico, Guatemala, Honduras, Panama, El Salvador and Peru; credit and retail expansion in Latin America.
rationale: Mexico City Grand Prix gives Elektra and Banco Azteca high visibility with their core mass-market customers.

desc: Operates Academy Sports + Outdoors stores selling sporting goods, outdoor gear, apparel and footwear in the southern and eastern US.
markets: United States only; opening new stores in the south and east.
rationale: Texas-based retailer near the Austin race could use F1 apparel tie-ins and customer hospitality.

desc: Publishes and distributes tabletop games including Catan, Ticket to Ride, Dobble and Pandemic across over 60 countries.
markets: Sells to stores in Europe, North America and Asia; expanding digital versions of its game brands.
rationale: Strong licensing and fan-engagement fit with motorsport games, such as F1-themed tabletop titles, and global family audience.

desc: Japanese food maker best known for Kewpie mayonnaise, dressings and egg products, with factories in the US, Asia and Europe.
markets: Japan, China, Southeast Asia, the US and Europe; growing salad dressing and egg products overseas.
rationale: Kewpie mayonnaise has global culinary reach; Suzuka and US races could build awareness, though marketing is food-focused.

desc: British producer of pork, chicken and premium food products supplying UK supermarkets, with some European and Asian exports.
markets: United Kingdom mainly, with exports to Europe and Asia; expanding premium and convenience food ranges.
rationale: British food supplier to supermarkets; Silverstone hospitality possible for retail customers, but brand marketing is minimal.

desc: Australian retailer of furniture, electrical goods and computers, operating franchised Harvey Norman stores in Australia and abroad.
markets: Australia, New Zealand, Ireland, Singapore, Malaysia and Slovenia; opening more overseas stores.
rationale: Melbourne Grand Prix provides local brand visibility, and franchise network hosting; an overseas tie-in is limited.

desc: Builds automated warehouse and online grocery technology for retailers such as Kroger and part-owns the Ocado Retail grocery delivery business.
markets: Partners in the UK, US, Canada, France, Spain, Japan, Australia and South Korea; expanding robotic fulfilment worldwide.
rationale: Robotics and logistics showcase to retail partners; F1 hospitality could host grocery-chain executives and demonstrate technology credentials.

desc: Japanese maker of oral care, laundry and household products including Clinica toothpaste and Kirei Kirei hand soap, sold across Asia.
markets: Japan, Thailand, Singapore, Malaysia, China and Korea; expanding in Southeast Asia.
rationale: Regional household brand could use Suzuka and Singapore races to reach Asian families, but spending is modest.

desc: Japanese frozen food and cold-chain logistics company selling processed foods, seafood and meat, with operations in Europe and Asia.
markets: Japan, Europe, Thailand, China and Australia; growing its cold-storage logistics network.
rationale: Mostly B2B food and logistics with limited consumer marketing, so F1 relevance is weak.

desc: Sells lawn and garden products under Scotts, Miracle-Gro and Roundup brands, mostly through US home-improvement retailers.
markets: United States and a small Canadian business; no verified expansion plans.
rationale: US consumer garden brands could hold US race activations, but the audience fit is poor and finances are strained.

desc: Sells a2 Milk-branded milk and infant formula made with A2 beta-casein protein, mainly in China, Australia and New Zealand.
markets: China, Australia, New Zealand, the United States and Southeast Asia; expanding in Asian infant formula markets.
rationale: Chinese and Australian consumer brand could use Melbourne Grand Prix and Chinese race visibility for premium nutrition.

desc: Operates online marketplaces and classifieds including Finn.no in Norway and Blocket in Sweden, formerly the Schibsted marketplace business.
markets: Norway and Sweden, with Nordic marketplace partnerships; investing in payments and AI-based search.
rationale: Nordic online classifieds brand could connect with Scandinavian fans, but audience is mostly domestic.

desc: Provides e-commerce growth technology and services that run online storefronts and marketplace sales for consumer brands, mainly on Amazon.
markets: United States, Europe and Asia marketplaces; expanding presence in Amazon and other marketplaces.
rationale: Brand-partner showcase for e-commerce clients; F1 provides a technology and global brand audience, but company is newly listed.

desc: Swedish retailer of hardware, electronics, home and leisure products operating Clas Ohlson stores in the Nordics and the UK.
markets: Sweden, Norway, Finland, Denmark and the UK; expanding online sales and Nordic stores.
rationale: Nordic home brand could use Swedish fans' F1 interest, but the company relies on low-cost retail.

desc: Makes branded cereals including Honey Bunches of Oats and Pebbles, plus refrigerated foods, eggs and pet food in North America.
markets: United States, Canada and some European markets; acquiring food companies.
rationale: US breakfast brands could target families at Austin and Miami, but F1 appeal is marginal.

desc: Operates Mercari, a Japanese online flea-market app for used goods, with a US service and a fintech arm.
markets: Japan and the United States; expanding Mercari app services.
rationale: Young app audience in Japan and the US; Suzuka and US races give brand awareness, but marketing is digital-first.

desc: Japanese meat and processed food producer, selling ham, sausages and chicken in Japan, Australia, Europe and the US.
markets: Japan, Australia, Thailand, Europe and the US; expanding its overseas meat business.
rationale: Meat brand with Asian and Australian sales; Suzuka and Melbourne audiences offer reach, but ties to F1 are unclear.

desc: Supplies sweeteners, fibres, texturants and stevia ingredients to food and beverage makers from plants in Europe, Americas and Asia.
markets: Sells to food and drink makers worldwide, particularly North America, Europe and Asia; investing in specialty food ingredients.
rationale: B2B ingredient business could host customers at Silverstone, but gains little consumer brand value.

desc: Makes fresh refrigerated pet food sold in US, Canadian and UK stores under the Freshpet brand.
markets: United States, Canada, the UK and Germany; expanding refrigerated pet food in Europe.
rationale: Pet owner audience is far from the F1 fan base, though US race activations could support brand awareness.

desc: Indonesian maker of household, food and personal care products such as Rinso, Sunsilk and Royco, sold mainly in Indonesia.
markets: Indonesia only; focus on mass-market household brands.
rationale: Unilever's global marketing could extend to F1, but this local unit sells to mass-market Indonesians and has no race.

desc: Spanish discount supermarket chain operating DIA and Clarel stores, mainly in Spain and Argentina after divesting other markets.
markets: Spain and Argentina; reorganised after selling Portugal, Brazil and France operations.
rationale: Discount-led domestic grocer with limited marketing budget; Spanish Grand Prix visibility offers little advantage.

desc: Japanese retail and credit-card group running Marui department stores and Epos credit cards, targeting young and urban consumers.
markets: Japan only; no verified expansion plans.
rationale: Young-shopper focus and credit card business offer a Suzuka audience, but little global scope.

desc: Japanese electronics retailer operating Yamada Denki stores selling appliances, computers and home goods, plus housing and furniture businesses.
markets: Japan only; diversifying into housing and furniture.
rationale: Appliance retailer with domestic focus; Suzuka hospitality is possible for suppliers, but brand fit is weak.

desc: Japanese discount retailer operating Trial stores, using retail data and AI to run low-cost supermarkets and smart-store technology.
markets: Japan only; rolling out smart-retail technology to more stores.
rationale: Technology-driven retail showcase to suppliers; limited F1 relevance given the low-price, domestic positioning.

desc: Produces and sells rice and pasta under brands including Riviana, Panzani, Tilda and Brillante in Europe, North America and Asia.
markets: Spain, France, the US, the UK and India; adding rice and pasta brand acquisitions.
rationale: Pasta and rice brands could use Monza and Miami visibility; Barilla already shows pasta fits F1.

desc: Runs CarGurus, an online car marketplace connecting buyers with dealers, with price analysis, in the US, Canada and the UK.
markets: United States, Canada and the UK; building wholesale and digital retail services for dealers.
rationale: Online car shoppers are a natural F1 audience; the company could use race weekends for dealer hospitality and Silverstone brand work.

desc: Largest US producer and seller of shell eggs, selling fresh and specialty eggs to retailers and food service customers.
markets: United States only; adding egg production and prepared foods.
rationale: Commodity egg producer with little consumer brand marketing; F1 relevance is minimal.

desc: Operates Topgolf entertainment venues and, until recent separation, Callaway golf clubs, balls and apparel sold worldwide.
markets: United States, Europe, Japan, Korea; Topgolf venues expanding in the US, UK and other markets.
rationale: Topgolf venues and golf equipment align with sports entertainment, hospitality and fan engagement, with US and UK F1 weekends.

desc: Makes salad dressings, sauces and frozen breads including Marzetti, Olive Garden dressings and New York Bakery, mainly for the US.
markets: United States only; no verified expansion plans.
rationale: US grocery and foodservice dressing maker; F1 offers little reach for these low-profile food brands.

desc: Makes Bic ballpoint pens, lighters and razors and Tipp-Ex products, sold to consumers in more than 160 countries.
markets: Sells in Europe, North America, Latin America, Africa and Asia; building out Bic Cristal and Flair brands.
rationale: Global consumer brand with sports sponsorship history; Bic lighters and razors link to F1 fans in Europe and Latin America.

desc: Makes and distributes lawn, garden and pet supplies including Nylabone, Kaytee, Pennington and Nutri-Source across US retailers.
markets: United States and Canada; acquiring pet and garden brands.
rationale: Pet and garden consumer goods with low F1 relevance beyond potential US retailer hospitality.

desc: Distributes natural, organic and conventional groceries to retailers across the United States and Canada, including Whole Foods Market.
markets: United States and Canada; serving natural grocery retailers.
rationale: Wholesale grocer with limited consumer brand; hospitality could target retailer partners but is not a strong fit.

desc: Holding company that controls Bel Group, the maker of Babybel, The Laughing Cow and Kiri cheeses sold worldwide.
markets: Via Bel Group: France, the US, Middle East, North Africa and Asia; expanding plant-based and snack cheese.
rationale: Cheese brands like Babybel could do family and European fan promotion, but a holding company is not an operating brand.

desc: Japanese toy maker behind Takara Tomy brands including Tomica, Beyblade and Pokemon toys, sold across Asia, Europe and North America.
markets: Japan, North America, Europe, China and Southeast Asia; expanding licensed toy and entertainment brands.
rationale: Tomica die-cast cars and Beyblade suit F1 licensed toys and young fan engagement; Mattel already shows the fit.

desc: Makes specialty and value-added food products including sandwiches, meat snacks and seafood, with operations in Canada, the US and Europe.
markets: Canada, the US and Europe; acquiring food companies in North America.
rationale: Mainly B2B specialty food supplier; Montreal and Austin races could host customers but F1 is not a natural match.

desc: Israel's largest supermarket chain, operating Shufersal Deal, Sheli and Yesh stores, and an online grocery business.
markets: Israel only; growing online and discount stores.
rationale: Domestic grocer; no Israeli race, so F1 reach is weak.

desc: Norwegian producer of farmed Atlantic salmon and trout, selling fresh and processed fish in Europe, Asia and the US.
markets: Sells salmon to Europe, Asia and North America; processing plants in Norway, Poland and Turkey.
rationale: Seafood producer with little consumer brand; Monaco or Miami hospitality for export customers is possible but unlikely.

desc: Holding company for CJ Group, which owns food business CJ CheilJedang, logistics, entertainment and bio units in Korea and abroad.
markets: South Korea, the US, China, Southeast Asia and Europe; Bibigo food brand expanding globally.
rationale: Group brands like Bibigo and CJ ENM could use the Korean Wave audience, but this is a holding company.
flags: holding / investment vehicle, not an operating brand

desc: Farms salmon in the Faroe Islands and Scotland and sells fresh and processed fish in Europe, Asia and the US.
markets: Sells to Europe, the US, China and Asia; expanding processing and farming in the Faroe Islands and Scotland.
rationale: Premium salmon producer with limited consumer presence; F1 hospitality could reach export buyers in Monaco and Miami.

desc: Operates Sheng Siong supermarkets in Singapore, with a few stores in China, selling groceries and fresh food to local households.
markets: Singapore, with small expansion in Kunming, China; no verified further expansion.
rationale: Singapore Grand Prix gives local visibility, but cost-conscious grocery brand rarely invests in international sport.

desc: Operates about 1,100 Kohl's department stores and a website selling apparel, shoes, home goods and beauty products in the US.
markets: United States only; adding Sephora shops and growing online sales.
rationale: US family shopper base and Sephora tie-ins could support Austin and Miami fan promotions, though the retailer is struggling.

desc: Sells furniture, mattresses and home decor through Bob's Discount Furniture stores and online in the northeastern and mid-Atlantic United States.
markets: United States only; adding stores across the east coast.
rationale: Regional furniture chain with TV-led marketing; limited global reach, though US race promotions are plausible.

desc: Australian wholesale distributor supplying IGA supermarkets, liquor stores and hardware retailers such as Mitre 10 across Australia.
markets: Australia only; growing its independent grocery, liquor and hardware wholesale networks.
rationale: Melbourne Grand Prix could host independent retailer partners, but brand-building value is limited.

desc: Brazilian cash-and-carry wholesaler operating Assai Atacadista stores serving households and small businesses across Brazil.
markets: Brazil only; opening new stores.
rationale: Sao Paulo Grand Prix visibility offers brand awareness among Brazilian shoppers, but low-price positioning is a weak fit.

desc: Japanese dairy company making Morinaga milk, yoghurt, infant formula and ice cream, with some business in the US and Asia.
markets: Japan, the US, China and Southeast Asia; growing infant formula and nutrition abroad.
rationale: Consumer dairy brand could use Suzuka exposure and family audiences, though F1 is not a natural channel.

desc: Europe's largest sugar producer, also making starch, bioethanol, frozen foods and fruit preparations through Suedzucker, Freiberger and CropEnergies.
markets: Europe, with operations in the US, Asia and Australia; investing in specialty foods and bioethanol.
rationale: Largely B2B food ingredient and ethanol business; F1 hospitality for industrial customers could work but brand value is low.

desc: Operates Japanese retail stores and supermarkets under the Blue Zones name, apparently focused on health-oriented foods.
markets: Japan only; no verified expansion plans.
rationale: Small recently listed retailer with unclear marketing capacity; F1 relevance is minimal.

desc: Operates MediaMarkt and Saturn consumer electronics stores across Europe, selling devices and appliances online and in shops.
markets: Germany, Spain, Italy, the Netherlands, Poland, Turkey and other European markets; growing marketplace and services.
rationale: Strong brand in Germany and Europe with technology suppliers; German-speaking fans and electronics partners suit F1 sponsorship.

desc: Japanese snack maker best known for Calbee potato chips and Frugra cereal, selling in Japan, North America, Asia and Europe.
markets: Japan, North America, China and Southeast Asia; expanding Frugra and potato snack sales abroad.
rationale: Snack brand reaches young fans in Japan and the US; Suzuka and US races offer natural promotion.

desc: Makes consumer goods including Sharpie pens, Rubbermaid storage, Coleman outdoor gear, Graco baby products and Yankee Candle.
markets: United States, Canada, Europe and Latin America; restructuring and cutting costs.
rationale: Many consumer brands could be activated at US race weekends, but financial pressure limits sponsorship spend.

desc: Sells luxury furniture, lighting and home furnishings through large galleries, catalogues and online in the US, Canada and Europe.
markets: United States, Canada and Europe; opening large galleries and a hospitality line.
rationale: Affluent customer base and design-led brand fit premium F1 hospitality, though RH has little sports marketing history.

desc: Canadian food processor making Maple Leaf, Greenfield and Lightlife meat, plant-based and prepared foods for Canada, the US and Asia.
markets: Canada, the United States and Asia exports; expanding sustainable protein and pork exports.
rationale: Montreal Grand Prix could support Maple Leaf brand awareness in Canada, but company is not marketing-led.

desc: British homewares retailer selling furniture, curtains, bedding and decor through Dunelm stores and online across the UK.
markets: United Kingdom only; expanding online and larger stores.
rationale: UK home Grand Prix could give visibility, but brand is domestic value homeware.

desc: Thai home-improvement retailer operating HomePro and Mega Home stores selling furniture and home goods in Thailand and Malaysia.
markets: Thailand, Malaysia and Indonesia (partner stores); growing in Malaysia.
rationale: Thai consumer brand in an F1-adjacent market could use regional race visibility, but home-retail spend is cautious.

desc: Operates Alfamart convenience stores across Indonesia and the Philippines, selling groceries and daily goods through thousands of outlets.
markets: Indonesia and the Philippines; continuing store expansion in both countries.
rationale: Mass-market convenience brand for Southeast Asian shoppers; no Indonesian race, so F1 relevance is thin.

desc: Operates Mr D.I.Y. discount stores selling hardware, household goods and toys across Malaysia, Indonesia, Brunei and Vietnam.
markets: Malaysia, Indonesia, Brunei, the Philippines and Vietnam; opening stores in Southeast Asia.
rationale: Value retailer with ambition in Southeast Asia, but F1 sponsorship is expensive for its price-focused model.

desc: Indian dairy company selling milk, curd, ice cream and Arun, Ibaco and Hatsun brand products in southern India.
markets: India, mainly southern states, with some exports; no verified expansion plans.
rationale: Regional dairy brand with no Indian race, so F1 offers little marketing logic.

desc: Runs GigaCloud, a business-to-business online marketplace for bulky goods such as furniture, serving buyers in the US, Europe and Asia.
markets: United States, Europe, Japan and Asia, with sellers largely in China and Vietnam; expanding cross-border marketplace and logistics.
rationale: Global B2B platform; F1 offers technology showcase and hospitality for sellers and retailers, but spending capacity is modest.

desc: South African food maker selling bread, grains, snacks and Jungle oats, Koo and Albany brands across southern and West Africa.
markets: South Africa, Nigeria, Ethiopia and other African markets; expanding in Nigeria and East Africa.
rationale: African consumer brand with no African race; limited fit for F1 though Las Vegas could showcase brands.

desc: Makes roof boxes, bike racks, strollers and bags for outdoor and travel, selling Thule brand products in over 130 countries.
markets: Europe, North America and Asia; growing in bicycle and baby products.
rationale: Global brand serving drivers and active families fits F1 audiences in Europe and the US, with car-accessory tie-ins.

desc: Japanese food ingredient group producing soy protein, specialty oils, chocolate and fats, with plants in Asia, Europe and the US.
markets: Japan, Southeast Asia, the US, Europe and China; expanding in plant-based protein.
rationale: B2B ingredients limit brand appeal, though Suzuka hospitality could host food-industry clients.

desc: Thai conglomerate making consumer goods and packaging and operating Big C hypermarkets and other retail across Thailand and Vietnam.
markets: Thailand, Vietnam, Laos and Cambodia; expanding Big C stores and consumer goods.
rationale: Thai mass-market retail brand could use regional F1 interest, though group marketing focuses on retail promotion.

desc: British food maker producing Mr Kipling, Bisto, Oxo, Ambrosia and Batchelors brands sold mainly in UK supermarkets.
markets: United Kingdom, with exports to Australia, Canada and Ireland; developing the Mr Kipling brand abroad.
rationale: Household UK food brands could reach family audiences at Silverstone, but business is mainly domestic.

desc: Indian food business selling Fortune cooking oil, flour, rice and other staple foods, plus industrial agri products.
markets: India, with some exports; no verified expansion plans.
rationale: Large Indian consumer staple brand, but no Indian race limits relevance.

desc: Thai retailer of mobile phones, computers and accessories, distributing Apple products and operating Com7 and iStudio stores across Thailand.
markets: Thailand, with some operations in Laos and Cambodia; no verified expansion plans.
rationale: Technology retailer for Thai consumers; F1 offers tech brand tie-ins via suppliers, but domestic scale limits spend.

desc: Japanese seafood and frozen food company producing fish products, fish oil and chilled foods in Asia, Europe and the Americas.
markets: Japan, the US, Europe, Chile and Southeast Asia; expanding aquaculture and processed foods.
rationale: Seafood supplier with limited consumer brand; F1 promotion is secondary to its B2B business.

desc: Operates Hornbach DIY megastores and garden centres selling building materials and home improvement goods in Germany and eight other countries.
markets: Germany and eight European countries; opening further stores in central and eastern Europe.
rationale: Germany's strong home-improvement customer base is an F1 audience, though the company has used mainly non-motorsport marketing.

desc: Runs Supercheap Auto, Rebel Sport, BCF and Macpac stores selling auto parts and sporting and outdoor goods in Australasia.
markets: Australia and New Zealand; expanding store network and loyalty programmes.
rationale: Supercheap Auto and Rebel Sport link directly to motorsport fans, ideal for Melbourne Grand Prix marketing.

desc: Makes salty snacks including Utz potato chips, Zapp's, Golden Flake and Boulder Canyon sold across the United States.
markets: United States only; expanding in the western US.
rationale: US snack brands could hold race-weekend promotions, but business is domestic.

desc: Japanese retailer running Hankyu and Hanshin department stores and Izumiya supermarkets in the Kansai region.
markets: Japan, mainly Kansai; no verified expansion plans.
rationale: Regional department store; Suzuka hospitality is possible, but limited international or motorsport marketing.
